author: CinephileMax
title: A monument of modern cinema
body: Nolan orchestrates the Manhattan Project with the precision of its own subject. Cillian Murphy's performance is volcanic and restrained simultaneously â€” a career-defining turn that transcends biopic convention.

author: FilmStudent22
title: Technically masterful, emotionally complex
body: The triptych structure gives the film its peculiar power. The courtroom sequences drag slightly, but the Trinity test sequence is cinema at its most visceral.

author: TVCritic
title: The best show on television, by some distance
body: Season 2 Episode 7 'Forks' is the finest hour of television produced this decade. The Bear operates at an intensity that is physically uncomfortable to watch, in the best possible way.

author: SharpObserver
title: Shakespeare for the streaming age
body: The final season dismantled everything the show had built â€” that decision, controversial and brave, cements Succession as a tragedy in the classical tradition.

author: SandwormFan
title: Villeneuve delivers his magnum opus
body: Dune Part Two is everything the first film promised. The Harkonnen scenes shot in black-and-white infrared are genuinely unlike anything in modern blockbuster cinema.

author: HistoryBuff
title: Television event of the year
body: Shogun achieves the impossible â€” it makes the original miniseries feel incomplete by comparison. Hiroyuki Sanada has never been better, and that is saying something.
